method.cache: Warm-cache, no OS/cache flush; not a cold-start or throughput test
comparisonPlan: baseline-recheck by restoring the original index definitions
candidate-recheck by restoring the migration index definitions
method.presentation: Short performance note with tables and full plan artifacts

environment.postgres: PostgreSQL 16.15 on x86_64-amazon-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (GCC) 11.5.0 20240719 (Red Hat 11.5.0-5), 64-bit

existingIndexes.indexdef: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX conversation_members_conversation_id_user_id_unique ON public.conversation_members USING btree (conversation_id, user_id)
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX conversation_members_pkey ON public.conversation_members USING btree (id)
CREATE INDEX conversation_members_user_id_idx ON public.conversation_members USING btree (user_id)
CREATE INDEX messages_conversation_created_id_idx ON public.messages USING btree (conversation_id, created_at, id)
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX messages_pkey ON public.messages USING btree (id)
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX messages_sender_id_client_message_id_unique ON public.messages USING btree (sender_id, client_message_id)
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX users_pkey ON public.users USING btree (id)
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX users_username_unique ON public.users USING btree (username)

queries.name: directory-first
queries.sql: select "id", "username" from "users" "users" where "users"."id" <> $1 order by "users"."id" asc limit $2

queries.name: directory-middle
queries.sql: select "id", "username" from "users" "users" where ("users"."id" <> $1 and "users"."id" > $2) order by "users"."id" asc limit $3

queries.name: directory-deep
queries.sql: select "id", "username" from "users" "users" where ("users"."id" <> $1 and "users"."id" > $2) order by "users"."id" asc limit $3

candidateIndexes.indexdef: CREATE INDEX conversation_members_user_conversation_idx ON public.conversation_members USING btree (user_id, conversation_id)
CREATE INDEX users_directory_id_username_idx ON public.users USING btree (id, username)

checks: Identical ordered directory rows and unordered membership sets in all four phases
Directory self-exclusion within measured pages; exact nextCursor
Five actual service pages strictly ascending with no duplicate IDs
Tail page self-exclusion, null nextCursor, and empty page beyond last ID
Non-member history denied; member empty history preserved
Tracked migration applied twice without a second schema change
